Navigation

Navbar

Sticky site header: logo, text links and one call to action; wraps instead of overflowing (no drawer yet, roadmap P3.2).

Live example

The example needs JavaScript; the usage below shows the markup.

Usage

Sticky site header — the reusable primitive behind the site ui kit's bespoke SiteHeader. Translucent cream, blurred, thin bottom border.

<Navbar logoSrc="/assets/logos/wordmark-purple.svg" logoAlt="Rede Sesc de Educação"
  links={[{ label: 'Programas', href: '#programas' }, { label: 'Unidades', href: '#unidades' }]}
  activeHref="#programas" ctaLabel="Encontre uma unidade" ctaHref="#unidades" />

String/array props only (no icon or nested-component slots) so it drops straight into templates. For a fully custom header layout, compose IconButton/Button directly instead.

  • The row wraps; from 360px up nothing overflows. Below 48rem the links move to their own row under logo + call to action. Every link and the CTA are at least --rse-hit-target-min tall.
  • The link matching activeHref gets aria-current="page"; in plain HTML set it yourself.
  • Not included: a hamburger/drawer for narrow screens. That is roadmap P3.2 (SiteHeader with mobile nav); until then keep the link list short (about five).

Plain HTML:

<header class="rse-navbar">
  <div class="rse-navbar__inner">
    <img class="rse-navbar__logo" src="/assets/logos/wordmark-purple.svg" alt="Rede Sesc de Educação">
    <nav class="rse-navbar__links" aria-label="Principal">
      <a class="rse-navbar__link" href="#programas" aria-current="page">Programas</a>
      <a class="rse-navbar__link" href="#unidades">Unidades</a>
    </nav>
    <a class="rse-navbar__cta" href="#unidades">Encontre uma unidade</a>
  </div>
</header>

Pass logoDarkSrc with the official white lockup alongside the purple logoSrc when a page supports dark themes. CSS chooses the correct image using the nearest data-rse-theme setting (including nested light and auto mode). Both files are unchanged official assets; do not filter or recolour the logo. Plain HTML uses .rse-navbar__logo--light and --dark on the two images.

Props

PropTypeRequiredNotes
logoSrcstring—Logo image URL
logoDarkSrcstring—White lockup for dark surfaces. Optional; CSS follows the nearest explicit theme or auto mode
logoAltstring—Alt text for the logo
linksNavbarLink[]—Text links; they wrap onto their own row on narrow screens
activeHrefstring—The link whose href matches gets aria-current="page" and the primary colour
ctaLabelstring—Call-to-action label; omit for no button
ctaHrefstring—
onCtaClick() => void—

Also accepts every attribute of React.HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement>, a ref and className.

CSS classes

Blocks
.rse-navbar
Elements
.rse-navbar__cta .rse-navbar__inner .rse-navbar__link .rse-navbar__links .rse-navbar__logo
Modifiers
.rse-navbar__logo--dark .rse-navbar__logo--light

Component tokens

Set any of these on :root or an ancestor to re-skin Navbar without touching its CSS. Each defaults to a role token, so it follows the theme. Use a role or palette token as the new value, and keep its pairs in scripts/contrast-pairs.mjs passing.

TokenDefaultLightDarkContrast
--rse-navbar-bg{rse.color.surface-page-translucent}rgba(242,244,228,0.92)rgba(27,26,38,0.92)#ffffff
--rse-navbar-border{rse.color.border-subtle}#e4e2d9#34323f#5b5866
--rse-navbar-cta-bg{rse.color.primary}#6c62c4#8e82d8#4a3fa8
--rse-navbar-cta-fg{rse.color.text-on-primary}#ffffff#171622#ffffff
--rse-navbar-link{rse.color.text-body}#454235#cfcdc6#1a1926
--rse-navbar-link-active{rse.color.primary}#6c62c4#8e82d8#4a3fa8
